journey.name: Type and arrive
journey.idea: The system recognises the identifier and takes the person there in one step, telling them plainly when it cannot.
journey.outcome: Go straight to a known category, product, support definition or policy by typing its identifier.

stepDetails.intent: Name what is wanted by its identifier and arrive there.
stepDetails.system: Trims the text, resolves the kind in order and any suffix, then opens it as the outcome rules say, or says it was not found.
stepDetails.reason: Recognising and going are one action, saving a step.

today.what: Looks the typed ID up among categories, products, support definitions and policies and shows what it found
Asks for an identifier and moves to, or opens, the matching category, policy, product or support definition.
Takes the status icons from the main window's icon list

keeps.says: Text typed in Find by ID is trimmed and looked up in this order: category, product, support definition, then policy. The first kind that matches is selected, with its own icon shown; a policy is looked up only when no other kind matches.

A policy ID may end with "@U" to mean the user section or "@C" to mean the computer section; without a suffix, or with any other suffix, the policy applies to both sections. The suffix is cut off before the policy lookup, so an unknown suffix still finds the policy.

When the text matches nothing, nothing is selected and a "not found" icon is shown; when the text is empty a blank icon is shown instead. The section from an earlier match is not cleared when the text changes to a non-policy.
The area choice offers only "User or Computer", "User" and "Computer", with no free text.

After finding by identifier, a category opens if it is visible, otherwise the person is told "The category is not currently visible. Change the view settings and try again."; a policy opens in the editor and the list moves to it; a product or support definition opens its details; anything else gives "That object could not be found.".

Moving to a policy first shows its category, but only when that category is visible in the tree; otherwise nothing happens and the person is not told. The policy row is then selected only if the policy is listed there. A policy hidden by the area choice or the filter leaves the category shown with nothing selected and no message; find by text and by registry do not check this before opening the editor.
A policy found by identifier opens in the lower-numbered of the area shown and the area found (computer is lower than user, user lower than both), so Computer wins over User.
Only one item in the policy list can be selected at a time.

After the edit dialog is accepted, which changes the open policy source in memory only, the list is refreshed in place if the current category is still visible; otherwise the program moves up to the nearest visible category. Nothing is written to disk until Save Policies.

stepDetails.intent: Read the details of a product or support definition reached.
stepDetails.system: States the kind, parent, version, children, and how a support definition matches and lists its entries.
stepDetails.reason: Details are shown only for what has them, not as a dialog every time.

today.what: Asks for an identifier and moves to, or opens, the matching category, policy, product or support definition.

keeps.says: Each entry of a support definition is listed by the name of the nested support definition when it is one, otherwise by the name of the product, otherwise as "<missing: " followed by the product code the entry names. Minimum and maximum versions are listed only for product entries that name a version range; a missing bound is shown blank.
The product details window lists every child revision of a product with its version and name; a product with no children shows an empty list.
A product with a parent shows the parent name and enables the parent button; a product with no parent shows a blank parent and the button is disabled.
The product details window shows a version number for major and minor revisions only; for a top-level product the version is blank.
The product details window labels a product "Major revision", "Minor revision" or "Top-level product" from its type.

The support details window states how a support definition matches products: "Match all the referenced products", "Match any of the referenced products", or "Do not match products" when it has no matching logic.

ownComponents.name: Support evaluator
ownComponents.responsibility: Works out whether a support definition is met for chosen products.

enforces.says: A support entry for a product counts as met in two cases. The entry is not a version range and that exact product is among the chosen products. Or the product has versions beneath it, and any of those versions or their sub-products is chosen, even when the product itself is not.

A support entry for a product that has versions beneath it, whether a version range or a plain entry for a parent product that is not itself chosen, counts as met when any version in its range, or a sub-product directly beneath one, is chosen. The range runs from the entry's minimum (0 if none) to its maximum (the highest version if none). A range entry never matches on its own product, and a product with no versions beneath it never matches this way.

When the caller asks for 'any' matching, a support definition whose logic is all-of needs every entry met, and any other definition needs one entry met. When the caller does not ask for 'any', every definition, all-of included, is met by one entry. A definition with no entries, or none met, is met only when all are required. Plain product entries are checked before nested definitions.

A support definition met a second time anywhere in one evaluation counts as not met, because the list of definitions seen is never emptied. Two entries that point at the same definition, with no cycle, make the second one not met.
When a policy lists no supported-on information, it counts as supported only if the caller allows unlisted policies. The same applies to a support entry that names no known product.

ownComponents.name: Policy lookup
ownComponents.responsibility: Resolves an identifier to a policy, category, product or support definition and opens it.

ownComponents.name: Identifier Kind Resolver
ownComponents.responsibility: Trims the typed identifier, cuts off a section suffix and looks the kind up in the fixed order, policy last.

ownComponents.responsibility: Opens what was found as its kind requires, says when nothing is found, and shows the matching icon.

ownComponents.name: Single Selection Guard
ownComponents.responsibility: Keeps at most one item of the policy list selected.

enforces.says: Only one item in the policy list can be selected at a time.

usedComponents.name: Product browser
usedComponents.responsibility: Lists products with child counts and shows versions and details.

enforces.says: The major versions list shows the children of the selected top-level product ordered by version, with the heading naming that product; with no product selected it is empty and prompts the person to select one.
Opening product details by double-click or Enter does nothing when no product is selected in that list.

The minor versions list shows the children of the selected major version ordered by version, with the heading naming it; with no major version selected it is empty and prompts the person to select one.
Double-clicking a child revision in the product details window shows that child in the same window; with nothing selected, nothing happens.
The top-level products list shows every loaded product ordered by name, each with its number of children.
The product details window lists every child revision of a product with its version and name; a product with no children shows an empty list.
A product with a parent shows the parent name and enables the parent button; a product with no parent shows a blank parent and the button is disabled.
The product details window shows a version number for major and minor revisions only; for a top-level product the version is blank.
The product details window labels a product "Major revision", "Minor revision" or "Top-level product" from its type.

usedComponents.name: Support rule browser
usedComponents.responsibility: Filters support definitions and shows entries, with the products covered.

enforces.says: The support definitions list shows only definitions whose name contains the typed filter text, ignoring upper or lower case; an empty filter shows all. Entries are ordered by name with leading spaces ignored and shown without them.

Double-clicking an entry in the support details window opens the product details window for a product entry, and shows a nested support definition in the same window. An entry whose product is missing, or with nothing selected, does nothing.

Each entry of a support definition is listed by the name of the nested support definition when it is one, otherwise by the name of the product, otherwise as "<missing: " followed by the product code the entry names. Minimum and maximum versions are listed only for product entries that name a version range; a missing bound is shown blank.

The support details window states how a support definition matches products: "Match all the referenced products", "Match any of the referenced products", or "Do not match products" when it has no matching logic.

usedComponents.name: Category tree presenter
usedComponents.responsibility: Presents the category tree with visibility, icons, selection and area choice.

enforces.says: A category's icon is chosen in this order: orphaned, then empty, then normal.
A category is visible when empty categories are switched on. Otherwise it is visible only if it has at least one visible policy or one visible subcategory.
A category appears in the tree only when it passes the visibility rule; each shown category gets an icon by its kind and carries its visible subcategories below it, and the tree is sorted.
The category tree selection follows the category shown in the right pane.
After the category tree is rebuilt from the loaded definitions, no category, policy or highlighted item is selected and the information pane shows the empty state.
Selecting a category in the tree makes it the current category and clears any selected policy.
The "Empty Categories" menu switches empty categories on or off and the view moves to the nearest visible category.
The area choice "User" shows user policies, "Computer" shows computer policies and any other choice shows both.

When the list is rebuilt, the policy already selected is selected again and revealed only if it is still listed, that is, it sits in the category shown and passes the visibility rule; otherwise nothing is selected. Then, if the policy is in the same category and the list still has that many rows, the earlier top row is put back, so the policy is not guaranteed to stay in view.

usedComponents.name: Visible Category Follow
usedComponents.responsibility: After sources open or a view setting changes, moves to the nearest visible category and drops a selection that is no longer shown.

enforces.says: After the person chooses policy sources, they are opened with the opening result shown, and the view moves to the nearest visible category.

When a view setting changes, the program moves up to the nearest visible category, drops the selected policy if the move happened or the policy is now hidden, then rebuilds the tree and list. A policy kept after the move appears in the information pane only: rebuilding the list reselects the category in the tree, which clears the selection, so its row is not highlighted.

usedComponents.name: Policy inspector
usedComponents.responsibility: Gives a plain summary of a policy first and presentation and element detail on demand.

enforces.says: The policy inspector shows a "Registry value" line for the policy only when the policy names a registry value.
The policy inspector shows a "Client extension" line for the policy only when the policy names a client extension.

The policy inspector lists presentation details for the policy whenever it has both a presentation and elements, whatever the elements hold. Each presentation item with an ID is matched to the policy element with the same ID; items without an ID show no element details. When no element has that ID, the inspector stops with an unhandled error.
Choice display names in the inspector are resolved through the definitions file that defines the policy, and choices are numbered from zero in file order.

For a list element the inspector states how value names are formed: "User provides value names" when the person names them, a prefix when the element has one, otherwise "No prefix (values named for their data)".

In the inspector, a group of affected registry settings with no on or off setting reads "Left implicit" when the policy names a registry value, and "Left to elements" when it names none. Inside a Yes/No element it always reads "Left implicit".
The inspector copies the selected line to the clipboard only on Ctrl+C with a line selected.

usedComponents.name: Policy Edit Session
usedComponents.responsibility: Holds one open edit of a policy: the area, the writable check, the chosen state, the forecast, and how it ends as a change or a cancel.

enforces.says: When the policy setting dialog is closed by any other means, it is still reported as a change if Apply was used earlier.

A policy that applies to both computer and user can be edited for either, starting on Computer when no section was given; a policy for one section is fixed to that section and the section choice is unavailable.
OK and Apply are available only when the chosen policy source can be written to.
The state shown when the dialog opens follows the policy's present state in the source being edited: Enabled, Disabled, or Not Configured for anything else, including an unclear state.
OK writes the policy to the source and closes the dialog as a change.

Choosing Computer or User in the dialog switches the source, its writability and its comments to that section, and reloads the chosen state (Enabled, Disabled or Not Configured) from it. Option values are replaced only for options the section stores when it is Enabled; other values typed earlier stay in the controls.
Apply writes the policy to the source, keeps the dialog open and records that a change was made.
Closing the policy setting dialog with Cancel is reported as a change when Apply was used earlier in that session, and as a cancel otherwise.
Option controls can be edited only while Enabled is chosen; with Disabled or Not Configured they are greyed out.

After the edit dialog is accepted, which changes the open policy source in memory only, the list is refreshed in place if the current category is still visible; otherwise the program moves up to the nearest visible category. Nothing is written to disk until Save Policies.

When the policy is Enabled, each option control is set to the value found in the source: numbers into number boxes, text into text and combo boxes, the matching item in drop-downs, true or false into check boxes, lines into multi-line boxes and the stored list into the list editor.
The Supported on box shows the supported-on name of the policy and is empty when the policy names none.

Applying a policy first forgets everything the source holds for it; Enabled then writes every option's current value, Disabled writes the disabled state, and Not Configured leaves the policy with no values.

usedComponents.name: Policy details presenter
usedComponents.responsibility: Shows a policy's section, place and support with gaps flagged.

enforces.says: When a policy sits in a category that exists, the category name is shown and the category-details button is enabled. A policy whose named category is unknown shows "<orphaned from " followed by that category code, and one with no category code shows "<uncategorized>"; the button is then disabled.

When a policy names a support definition that exists, its name is shown and the support-details button is enabled. When it does not exist, the button is disabled and the text reads "<missing: " followed by the code the policy names; with no code the text is blank.
The policy details window names the section a policy applies to: "User or computer" when it applies to both, "Computer" when machine-only, "User" when user-only.

usedComponents.name: Category details presenter
usedComponents.responsibility: Shows a category with its chain of parents and policies.

enforces.says: The detail window of a category shows its parent's name and enables the parent button when the parent exists; when the parent is named but missing it shows "<orphaned from <parent>>" and the button is disabled; a top-level category shows nothing.
